• Decreases in snow cover have largely occurred in spring and summer, whereas winter snow cover has remained fairly steady since 1981 and fall snow cover has increased. Spring and summer snow cover can have a particularly important influence on water supplies.
  • Snow-covered area is projected to continue to decrease in all seasons under all four greenhouse gas emissions scenarios. Snow cover could stabilize by late in this century under the low emissions scenario, where there are significant reductions in greenhouse gas and other air pollutant emissions. It will continue to decrease under the other three scenarios, however. Higher emissions lead to less snow cover.
